text:
### Observed differences

- The dominant difference is a rerouting around A40, A21 and the chain A22–A23–A27. In the earlier window, A40 was followed directly by A21 in all 200 traces, while the either/or step (exactly one of A14, A15, A20 per case) sat inside the later chain: A22 led to A23 in about 48 of 100 transitions and to one of A14/A15/A20 otherwise, A23 led to A27 in about 53 of 100 and to one of the three otherwise, and A14/A15/A20 exited to A23 or A27 in roughly equal shares. In the later window, A40 leads to A14 (about 34 in 100), A15 (about 35) or A20 (about 31); each of the three leads to A21 in every observed transition (68, 69 and 63 transitions); and A22 → A23 → A27 is now a direct chain, each edge observed in 100 of 100 transitions. [DIR029, DIR010, DIR011, DIR016, DIR018, DIR019]

- Order, distance and position evidence agrees with this rerouting. A14 and A21 co-occurred in about 38 of 100 traces earlier, always with A21 first; later they co-occur in about 34 of 100, always with A14 first; against A22 the order flipped the same way, and A14 vs A23 went from mixed order (about 19 of 100 each way) to always A14 first. A40 and A21 were adjacent in every trace earlier and one event apart later; A22→A23 and A23→A27 had a one-event gap in roughly half the traces earlier and are adjacent in all traces later; A22→A27 shortened from three events to two. A14, A15 and A20 moved from a mean event position of about 0.60 of the trace to about 0.32, while A21, A22 and A23 shifted only about 0.01–0.03 later and A27 and A40 stayed in place. [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

- Participation of the three alternatives is essentially unchanged: A14 appears in about 38 of 100 traces earlier and 34 later, A15 in about 32 and 35, A20 in about 31 and 32, and the three never occur in the same trace in either window, so exactly one of them still executes per case. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC019, REL001, REL002, REL008]

- Repetition decreased around A10/A11 and A41: A10 and A11 still occur in every trace, but mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.9 to about 1.6 and traces containing a repeat fell from about 47 to 38 in 100; A41 fell from about 1.6 to 1.4 occurrences (repeats from about 38 to 30 in 100); A11 also routes to A10 less often (about 47 vs 36 of its outgoing transitions). [OCC009, OCC010, OCC026, DIR009]

- Routing shares shifted inside the A16–A19 cluster: A27 enters via A19 more often (about 19 vs 27 in 100) and via A16 less often (about 28 vs 20); the exit to A28 happens less often from A19 (about 62 vs 40) and more often from A16 and A17 (about 46 vs 52 and 43 vs 53); A16 participation fell from about 50 to 42 in 100 traces while A17 rose from about 50 to 58. Smaller shifts of the same kind appear around A34–A37 (exits to A29) and from A42/A44 to A45, and A13 participation fell from about 33 to 28 in 100 traces. [DIR020, DIR012, DIR013, DIR015, OCC015, OCC016, DIR024, DIR026, DIR031, DIR032, OCC012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the either/or step — exactly one of A14, A15 and A20 per case, with stable participation — changed its placement: in the earlier window it was inserted between A22/A23 and A23/A27, interrupting that chain while A40 connected directly to A21; in the later window it runs between A40 and A21, and A22, A23 and A27 execute as an uninterrupted A22 → A23 → A27 sequence. [DIR029, DIR010, DIR011, DIR016, DIR018, DIR019, REL003, REL004, LAG001, LAG004, POS001]

Supporting signs: the successor profiles of A14, A15, A20, A40, A22 and A23 were completely replaced rather than partially shifted (for example A14 went from A23/A27 about 50/50 to A21 in 100 of 100 transitions, on 76 vs 68 observed transitions), each with an empirical strength of about 0.995, so larger differences occurred in fewer than 1 of 200 random re-splits; the order flips, event-distance changes and position shifts all point the same way and are quantitatively consistent with a single move (A21 and A22 shift later by about one event while A27 stays put). The many items are therefore facets of one rerouting rather than independent confirmations, and because participation of every involved activity is stable, this is not a change in how often the step is used. [DIR010, DIR029, REL003, LAG004, POS004, POS007, OCC013]

Limitations: the indicators use event positions, so placement means order within the trace, not clock time; the evidence covers only outgoing sides and pairwise relations, so what precedes A40 and A22 is not observed; no screening baseline for chance expectations is included, so the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of the items; and two independent rewirings (A40 gaining the alternatives as successors while they lost their A22/A23 exits) would produce the same edge set as a single move — the coordinated position and distance shifts make a single move the more parsimonious reading, but the evidence cannot exclude this alternative. [DIR029, POS004, LAG004]

Other differences: not part of this hypothesis — repetition of A10 and A11 decreased (mean occurrences per trace about 1.9 to 1.6, still present in every trace) and of A41 slightly, with A11 routing to A10 less often; routing shares within the A16–A19 cluster and, more weakly, around A34–A37 and A42/A44 changed; A13 participation fell. These small share shifts could still be sampling variation between two 200-trace windows. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC026, DIR009, DIR020, DIR012, DIR015, OCC012]
